chunks: I asked him about a man who did not know whether he had prayed two rak'ahs or three. He said, “He repeats [the prayer].” I said, “Is it not said that a faqih does not repeat the salat (prayer)?” So he said, “That only applies to [doubt between] three and four.”
So it is to be understood as referring to salat al-maghrib, because we have already explained that whenever a person doubts in it, it is obligatory upon him to restart the salat (prayer).
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.الثَّلَاثِ وَالْأَرْبَعِ: doubt between the third and fourth rak'ah
key_terms.ثَلَاثًا: three units, in the context of doubt in prayer count

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone doubts whether they prayed two rak'ahs or three in salat al-maghrib?
ai.summary: This text discusses the ruling on doubt in the number of rak'ahs in salat (prayer), distinguishing between doubt involving two and three and doubt involving three and four. It further clarifies that the ruling of repeating the prayer is carried upon salat al-maghrib, in which doubt necessitates restarting the prayer.
